title: fix(spec,driver-turso)!: refuse encryptionKey on a local or replica turso datasource instead of writing the file in plaintext
body:
Fixes #25020
Clause-②: no (narrowing)

The `Clause-②` line above is the claim's (comment 6306742426: "If the measured route is the refusal, it is `no (narrowing)`"), and the measured route is the refusal. The changeset carries the same value. Under the claim, this PR owes a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review before the queue.

Dev run of the `domain:engine` seat 2 PM dispatch (session `session_01QK6pdbxKZiHdFApL8RYVh9`, `mode:subagent`), branch `claude/issue-25020-turso-encryption-key-local`, BASE `4d991588f`, with one true merge of `origin/main` at `d15981a07` (it touched no file of this diff). **Patch round 1** (contract review 6308116467, FAIL item 1 and findings 7–9; seat verdict 6308149967) landed as `0833772a4`, `b0236c662` and `4a595ed43`. **Patch round 2** (seat order 6310662118) landed as `df6803d15`: one changeset sentence, `.changeset/**` only. **Every reading below was taken at head `4a595ed43`** unless it says otherwise (the full dogfood battery, the derived gates and the check-runs were re-read at `df6803d15`); the H1 table and the H2 grep were read at BASE and at `d15981a07`, and nothing since touched what they read. Only test values appear here (`test-key-25020`); no real key and no production path.

## The premise, measured first: it does not hold

The seat's premise P was: the key can be honoured by handing it to the engine `driver-turso` already uses for the file's reads and writes, with no engine swap and no new dependency. Measured:

- **The engine is better-sqlite3 13.0.3 (SQLite 3.53.4), and it has no encryption codec.** `PRAGMA compile_options` lists no codec option. `PRAGMA key = 'test-key-25020'`, `PRAGMA cipher`, `PRAGMA cipher_version` and `PRAGMA rekey` all answer `[]` (an unknown pragma is a silent no-op). A table written after `PRAGMA key` leaves a file whose header is `SQLite format 3`, and a second, key-less read-only open reads the row back.
- **The native libSQL binding does encrypt** (`@libsql/client` 0.18.0 over `libsql` 0.5.29, already a dependency). A local `file:` client with the key writes a file whose header is not `SQLite format 3`; better-sqlite3 opening it answers `SQLITE_NOTADB`; a libSQL client reopening it without the key answers `SQLITE_NOTADB`; with the key it reads the row. But that binding is not the engine this driver reads and writes through, so honouring the key means replacing the Knex / better-sqlite3 path with another engine. That is the ruling's "P does not hold" branch.

So the route is the refusal. No engine swap, no partial swap, no warn-and-ignore.

## What the driver did with the key, per mode (H1), before this change

Measured on `TursoDriver` from source at BASE, with a test key:

| Mode | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| local (`file:` url + key) | constructs, connects, `syncSchema` + `create` + `find` round-trip; file header `SQLite format 3`; plain better-sqlite3, read-only, no key, reads the row |
| replica, supplied client (`file:` + `syncUrl` + `client`) | the same: the key reaches nothing |
| replica, driver-built sync client (`file:` + `syncUrl`, unreachable local sync endpoint) | `super.connect()` writes the file in plaintext first (`db.db`, `-shm`, `-wal`, header `SQLite format 3`); only then is `createClient` handed the key, and its construction fails to connect (`sync error: … tcp connect error`) |
| `@libsql/client` + the key, over that plaintext file | `SQLITE_NOTADB` |
| this driver's replica face over a file `@libsql/client` encrypted with the key | `DATABASE_ERROR` (`SQLITE_NOTADB`) |

So both halves of H1 hold, depending on which side opens the file with the key: the engine that serves every read and write never encrypts it, and a file the sync client encrypted is one that engine cannot open. **NOT MEASURED: a replica with the key against a reachable sync server.** No libSQL sync server runs in this container, and the native binding's default (non-offline) sync path speaks the server's replication protocol, which nothing here can stand in for. The refusal does not depend on it: it fires at construction, before any client is built.

## Who declares the key today (H2)

Measured on this tree at `d15981a07`: `git grep` over `examples/**`, `packages/create-objectstack`, `packages/cli/src` (non-test) and `skills/**` finds **zero** `encryptionKey` authors; no environment variable (`TURSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `OS_DATABASE_ENCRYPTION*`) or host default sets it. The hits are the declarations themselves, docs describing them (`content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`, `docs/design/driver-turso.md`, the driver README), and test fixtures. Of the fixtures, the redaction suites author it on remote `libsql://` urls (unaffected), and two `metadata-protocol` suites carry it on a `file:` url in STORED rows that no parse reads (run green, below).

## What changes

A non-empty `encryptionKey` on a local datasource (a `file:` url or `:memory:`) or an embedded replica (a `file:` url beside `syncUrl`), detected or forced with `mode`, is refused at all three places a turso config is judged, with one message per mode:

- **Construction.** `new TursoDriver()` (and `createTursoDriver()`) throws `VALIDATION_ERROR` / 400 before `super()`, so no file is opened. It is the last of the local-engine refusals in the constructor, thrown through the existing envelope helper. The message comes from `localEncryptionKeyRefusal(mode)` in `packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-driver.ts`.
- **Authoring.** `tursoTransportIssues` in `packages/spec/src/data/driver/turso.zod.ts` gains a last arm in the local / replica branch: one `custom` issue on `encryptionKey`. It reaches `DatasourceSchema` (as `config.encryptionKey`), `validateDriverConfig`, `defineStack` / `os validate`, and a save or test connection through the datasource admin service.
- **The driver mirror** (`packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/spec/turso.zod.ts`) carries the same arm byte for byte.

**Patch round 1: the key is judged by where the database lives, not by the mode.** A forced `mode: 'remote'` answers first in `detectMode`, so `{ url: 'file:…', mode: 'remote', encryptionKey }` skipped every local-engine refusal, and `connect()` handed the local url to `createRemoteClient()`, which builds `createClient({ url, authToken, concurrency })` with no key. Measured on this head with the new constructor arm ablated (leg D below): it constructed and connected in `remote` mode, `syncSchema` + `create` + `find` round-tripped, the file's header read `SQLite format 3`, and plain better-sqlite3, read-only, with no key, read the row. With the arm: `VALIDATION_ERROR` / 400 at construction, and the file does not exist afterwards. Now refused at all three places:

- **Construction.** One mode-independent predicate before `super()`: a non-empty key beside a url that `namesLocalDatabase()` (a `file:` url in any letter case, or `:memory:`, the same scheme fold the driver uses everywhere). In a local or replica mode it throws the existing text (every url reaching that point is already a `file:` url or `:memory:`, because `localEngineDefect` refused the rest); under a forced remote mode it throws `remoteModeLocalEncryptionKeyRefusal(url)`. It runs after every forced-remote refusal, so a `syncUrl` or a lone `sync` beside it keeps its own message.
- **Authoring.** `tursoTransportIssues` gains a last arm in its remote branch: a `file:` url or `:memory:` beside a non-empty key raises one `custom` issue on `encryptionKey`, after the `timeoutMs` and `syncUrl` issues.
- **The mirror** carries the arm byte for byte. It declares no `mode`, so zod strips a forced one and the mirror judges `{ url: 'file:…', mode: 'remote', encryptionKey }` as the local database its url selects: it refuses it on `encryptionKey`, in the local arm's text. Its copy of the remote arm is unreachable through it and is kept for copy parity, like its other forced-mode branches. The parity table therefore judges the forced-remote rows by the constructor and the spec contract (verdict, key, and byte equality of the constructor's message with the spec's), and skips the mirror's verdict for them, as it does for every forced-mode row.

Two texts, one per variant; both name the mode, echo no url and no key, and keep the envelope:

> `encryptionKey` asks for this datasource's database file to be encrypted, but `url` is a local `file:` url, and `mode: 'remote'` runs every read and write of that file through the libSQL client this driver builds, which is handed no key: nothing would encrypt the file, so it would be written in plaintext that any SQLite reader opens without the key — the turso driver refuses this configuration when it starts. Nothing in this driver encrypts a local file. Drop `encryptionKey`, and encrypt the disk or volume the file lives on instead, or point `url` at a remote Turso database, whose storage encryption is the server's to configure, not this key's.

> `encryptionKey` asks for this datasource's database to be encrypted, but `url` names an in-memory database, and `mode: 'remote'` runs every read and write of it through the libSQL client this driver builds, which is handed no key: there is no file for the key to encrypt, so it would change nothing — the turso driver refuses this configuration when it starts. Drop `encryptionKey`.

The key is not forwarded to `createClient` in this shape: honouring it there would make a file's encryption depend on a transport override, a capability nothing pulls, and #25050 proposes retiring the key. A remote url (`libsql://`, `https://`, `ws(s)://`) with a key is still accepted; that mode is #25050's.

The message (local; the replica variant says "an embedded replica" and adds the parenthesis "the sync client shares that one file, and a file it encrypted could not be opened by that engine"):

> `encryptionKey` asks for this datasource's database file to be encrypted, but this datasource is a local database, which runs every read and write through a local SQLite engine that has no encryption codec: nothing would encrypt the file, so it would be written in plaintext that any SQLite reader opens without the key — the turso driver refuses this configuration when it starts. Nothing in this driver encrypts a local or replica file. Drop `encryptionKey`, and encrypt the disk or volume the file lives on instead, or keep the data in a remote Turso database, whose storage encryption is the server's to configure, not this key's.

It names the mode and what does encrypt. It names the datasource the way its siblings do ("this datasource"): the driver is never handed the datasource's name, and the boot path prefixes every build failure with `datasource 'NAME': connect failed —` (`datasource-connection-service.ts`), while the authoring issue sits at that datasource's `config.encryptionKey`. It echoes no url and no key.

**Order.** A url the engine cannot open, a lone `sync`, a forced replica with no `syncUrl`, a forced local mode beside a `syncUrl`, and under a forced remote mode a `syncUrl`, each keep their own refusal. A lone `sync` or a forced-remote `syncUrl` stays the spec's first issue, with the key's second. An empty `encryptionKey` is unset, as the loaders read it (`buildTursoDriverConfig` drops it), and is still accepted. A remote url is not judged (the claim puts the `libsql://` mode out of scope; see Acceptance notes).

**Text made true.** The `encryptionKey` describe in both schemas, its TSDoc, `TursoDriverConfig.encryptionKey`, the README, `docs/design/driver-turso.md` §10, the `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx` still-writable trade-off (turso's key left it: it was never "a capability the client genuinely honours"), the `STILL_WRITABLE_CREDENTIAL_KEYS` comment and (patch round 1) the module header of `datasource-credential-redaction.ts`, the TSDoc of `@objectstack/service-datasource`'s exported `TursoDriverConfigInput.encryptionKey`, and the QA checklist's turso expectation (write-accepted only on a remote datasource now). Patch round 1 also makes the describe in both schemas, the regenerated reference, `drivers.mdx`'s remote sentence, the README and the design doc true for a `file:` url or `:memory:` under a forced remote mode. The replica arm of `connect()` stops forwarding `encryptionKey` to `createClient`: a non-empty one can no longer reach it. The generated `content/docs/references/data/driver-turso.mdx` is regenerated (`check:generated --fix`, the one stale artifact; in patch round 1 again, then `gen:schema`, `gen:docs` and `check:docs` in that order, exit 0 at `4a595ed43`: "227 generated files in sync with packages/spec").

**Migration.** `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.turso-config-local-encryption-key-refused.ts` (ADR-0087 semantic entry), registered in the changeset's ADR-0087 marker as `registered turso-config-local-encryption-key-refused`. The changeset `.changeset/25020-turso-encryption-key-local.md` is `minor` for `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/driver-turso`, BREAKING, with the FROM / TO table (a forced-remote row added in patch round 1) and the one-line fix: delete `encryptionKey` from every turso datasource whose `url` is a `file:` url or `:memory:`. `@objectstack/service-datasource` is graded `patch` for its TSDoc: `check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base origin/main --event` (this body's `Clause-②` line) answered exit 0, "@objectstack/service-datasource: patch … NOT refused". A stored row in that shape now fails when its driver is built (`failed-degraded`, ADR-0062 D5). Patch round 1 dropped the connect-failure escape hatch from the entry's `reason` and from the changeset's ADR-0062 D5 sentence.

## Pins

- `packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-driver-local-encryption-key-refusal.test.ts` (new): local (`file:`, `FILE:`, forced `mode: 'local'`, `:memory:`, `createTursoDriver`) and replica (driver-built client, supplied client, forced `mode: 'replica'`) refusals as `code` + `status` + the mode's first sentence, each asserting no database file exists afterwards; the message names no url and no key. Controls: a local datasource with no key, one with an empty key, and a replica with no key each construct, connect, write and read back through the driver, and the file is a plain SQLite database with the row.
- `packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/spec/turso-config-constructor-parity.test.ts`: 16 new rows (8 refused on `encryptionKey`, 6 order rows, 2 empty-key accept rows); the byte-equality set now includes `encryptionKey`; floors at the measured counts (8 key rows, 3 of them replica, 31 copied-message rows).
- `packages/spec/src/data/driver/turso.test.ts`: the authoring refusal per mode, no echo, order (including the two-issue `sync` + key case), both authoring doors, controls, and the describe no longer promising AES-256.
- **Patch round 1.** Refusal file: `file:`, `FILE:` and `file:` + `timeout` under a forced remote mode (`code`, `status`, the first sentence, no file afterwards), `:memory:` and `file::memory:` (the in-memory sentence), `createTursoDriver` with no echo; controls: the same shape with no key, with an empty key, `:memory:` with no key, and a `libsql://` url with a key (auto-detected and forced remote) each construct in remote mode. Parity table: 5 rows refused on `encryptionKey` under a forced remote mode, 2 order rows (`syncUrl` first, a lone `sync` first, each two issues at the spec), 4 accept controls (`:memory:` and an empty key under a forced remote mode, `libsql://` with a key auto-detected and forced); floors 13 key rows, 5 of them forced-remote, 38 copied-message rows. Spec test: the file and in-memory variants, no echo, order, both doors, controls, and the describe naming the forced remote mode.
- Fixture triage: `driver-turso/src/spec/turso.test.ts`'s all-fields replica fixture drops the key (it pinned the branch this removes); `driver-placeholder-refusal.test.ts`'s turso `encryptionKey` row moves to a remote url, the one mode where a literal still parses, with a comment that it pins the placeholder judgement and not a remote mode honouring the key.

## Reverse verification (ablation), direction predicted before it ran

Each leg went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` on the committed head (anchor 1 to 0, blob changed, restore proven: blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty). All three suites resolve the mutated file from source, so no rebuild was needed.

| Leg | Mutation | Run | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | constructor: the refusal call replaced by a no-op | the new refusal file + the parity table | **25 failed** / 249 passed / 37 skipped: all 9 refusal cases and 16 parity cases (8 key rows times constructor verdict and byte equality) red; the 3 controls and every order row green |
| B | spec: the `encryptionKey` arm disabled | `spec/src/data/driver/turso.test.ts` + the placeholder family | **5 failed** / 123 passed: the 5 refusal cases red; controls, the describe pin and the placeholder family green |
| C | mirror: the same arm disabled | the parity table + the mirror's own test | **7 failed** / 287 passed / 37 skipped: the mirror verdict on the 6 unforced key rows and the `sync` + key row red; forced-mode rows skip the mirror by design |
| D (patch round 1, at `4a595ed43`) | constructor: the new predicate narrowed back to the old guard (`mode !== 'remote' && …`) | the refusal file + the parity table, plus the door-6 probe | predicted: the forced-remote refusal cases red, everything else green. **16 failed** / 299 passed / 47 skipped: the 6 forced-remote refusal cases (3 file, 2 in-memory, `createTursoDriver`) and 10 parity cases (5 rows times constructor verdict and byte equality) red; every control, every local / replica case and both forced-remote order rows green. The probe under the mutation reproduced door 6 (plaintext file, read with no key) |

Not ablated: the parity table's spec half through `packages/spec/dist` (each leg would need a spec rebuild); leg B ablates the same arm through source. The new remote arm in the spec and the mirror is not ablated in patch round 1 (the dispatch asked for one leg, over the constructor arm); the mirror's copy is unreachable through the mirror, so no run could turn it red.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 121 families at `4a595ed43` (two more than round 0: the `check-tenant-audit-census` pair). All 121 were run once after a full `turbo run build`, each exit code captured to a file before any pipe: all 121 answered 0. `--ran` reconciliation: "121 derived, 121 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN". `check:driver-conformance` reads "55 covered cell(s), 0 in the DEBT ledger, 0 exempt" at BASE, at `d15981a07` and at `4a595ed43`. The local-only `check-dev-prereqs` scan: exit 0. The PR's check-runs on `4a595ed43`, read once: 36 success, 6 skipped.

**Full dogfood battery** (the title carries `!` and the line carries `(narrowing)`), once, on the final head `df6803d15`, closure built per ① and run under the lock as `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test` with no shard and no path: `VERDICT command-exit 0`, Test Files 284 passed, 3 skipped (287), Tests 2361 passed, 18 skipped. No failure. (At `4a595ed43` the same battery also read `VERDICT command-exit 0`, 284 passed / 3 skipped, 2361 passed / 18 skipped.) At `df6803d15` the 121 derived gate families all exit 0 (`--ran`: 121 derived, 121 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN), and the check-runs read 36 success, 6 skipped.

## Acceptance notes

- **A remote url still accepts the key and drops it (not this card's; the claim puts the `libsql://` mode out of scope; filed as #25050).** Measured: `new TursoDriver({ url: 'libsql://db.example.invalid', encryptionKey: 'test-key-25020' })` constructs and connects in `remote` mode; `createRemoteClient` never forwards the key; `@libsql/client`'s own remote client refuses that key (`ENCRYPTION_KEY_NOT_SUPPORTED: Encryption key is not supported by the remote client.`). The spec contract parses it on a remote url. After this PR the key is honoured in no mode, which the describes now say. A local url under a forced remote mode is not this case: it is refused (patch round 1).
- The `encryptionKey` key stays declared (and redacted on read) because removing it is a key retirement this refusal does not make.
